name: Week 25 KB Thursday — 🌀 Outside Snatch Flow + Brutal Complex at the Right Bell
description:
**The Brutal Complex gets the run it never got.** Last week it opened at 50 against a 20-30 prescription, and that first round cost the block — rounds two and three ran at 35 on an empty tank. The bell is written as a number this week, not a range: **35, and rounds are the variable.**

**Outside Snatch Flow stays** — it's a confirmed keeper and the outside-arc snatch turned out to be a core move rather than a shoulder one. The spotlight moves off it.

**The KB curl joins Thursday too**, left arm first, same as Tuesday.

dayOverview.theme: The conditioning block repeats instead of rotating, for one specific reason: it was never actually run at the right bell. Opening at 50 turned three rounds into one honest round and two on empty. At 35 with rounds as the variable, the block finally gets to do its job. The Outside Snatch Flow stays as the keeper it's proven to be. Rotation happens on Tuesday this week instead.

spotlights.why: You named it yourself: the ab-stance squats and the close-grip pushups are what make the Brutal Complex brutal, and the swing and the row are basically rest. That's a useful pacing map and it also identifies the two moves worth actually coaching. The pushup is the one with a technique ceiling — hands on the bell handles, on an unstable object, with the elbows tucked. Done well it's a close-grip press with a stability tax. Done badly it's a shoulder-forward collapse onto a wobbling bell, which is the last thing the right shoulder needs at the end of a long day.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: Thursday content rotates: W22 Outside Snatch Flow + GymFiesta circuit · W24 Outside Snatch Flow + Brutal Complex · W25 same pairing, run at the correct bell (current) · W26 rotate the conditioning block — the cardio complex or the upper circuit. The Outside Snatch Flow is a confirmed keeper; cycle the second block around it.
watchpoints: **🌀 Brutal Complex at 35. Not a range — 35.** swing → ab-stance goblet squat → alternating bent-over row → close-grip pushup on the bell handles. Circuit-style, ~10-12 reps per move, ~60s between rounds.

**Rounds are the variable, not the bell.** Three rounds is the target; go past it if the block still has something left. **Stop a round when the hinge stops holding**, not when the clock says so — there's a bent-over row and loaded squats in there.
**🔆 Close-grip pushup on the bell: elbows TUCKED, shoulders packed DOWN, ribs down** 🛑. This is the beat with a technique ceiling.
**Pacing map (your read, and it's right): the squats and the pushups are the work. The swing and the row are the rest.** Spend your effort accordingly.
**🌀 Outside Snatch Flow — light bell, 2-3 rounds each side.** The spotlight rotates off; it's a known chain now. The outside-arc snatch reads as core, not shoulder — 35 ran fine for two extra rounds.
**KB curl, LEFT FIRST** 🔥, light bell. Same as Tuesday — this is the frequency, not the intensity.

**Strict overhead press holds 50 — with a 2-3s PAUSE AT LOCKOUT every rep** 🛑. 50 is the Arrilaga ceiling and it read "pretty easy" Tuesday, so the pause is the progression, not the bell. KB row holds 50 — maintenance.
**Bent press + windmill keep the skill slot** 🛑, unhurried, light.
**Intensity tags:** 🔥 near-failure OK — KB curl, and the complex's round count. 🛑 keep it shy — snatch, overhead press, bent press, windmill, the close-grip pushup.
**Banded shoulder prep + protective shrug stay in the warm-up.**

sets.name: Warm-Up (incl. Bottoms-Up Cuff Prep + Figure-8 Passes)
sets.notes: Light bell throughout. The figure-8 passes here are the coordination primer — the heavy version lives on Tuesday.

exercises.notes: Slow, close to the head. Shoulders packed down.
Light bell inverted. Cuff prep and grip.
**Light bell** — this is the coordination primer, not the 50lb Tuesday finisher. Hinge, don't squat.
Hinged slightly forward, tight fists, thumbs tucked.
Protective activation. Down and back at the top.

sets.name: Banded Shoulder Prep (~3 min)
sets.notes: 1 round of all 7 banded moves (~3 min). Sustained tension, no rest between positions.

sets.name: 🌀 Outside Snatch Flow — the Keeper
sets.notes:
**Single light bell (~25-35lb), 2-3 rounds each side.** Third run, and it's landed — 'so nice when i got it.'

figure-8 → tactical clean → transverse lunge → outside snatch → windmill → snatch → thruster → deep squat press → hand-to-hand swing.

- **The outside snatch is a CORE move**, which is what you found last time — the bell traveling off the midline makes it anti-rotation work, not shoulder work. Let the trunk resist the pull rather than muscling the arc
- **Punch the hand through** so the bell rolls onto the forearm instead of banging it
- **Pack the shoulder DOWN at every catch** 🛑
- **The chain shouldn't have stops in it** — you know the order now, so spend the attention on the transitions

35 ran fine for two extra rounds last week, so the bell can sit at the top of the light range.

sets.name: Strength — Row + Strict Press + KB Curl (Between the Big Blocks) 🛑
sets.notes: 3 rounds, run between the flow and the complex so the demanding volume isn't stacked at the top.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 50. Hinged, flat back, bell to the hip.
- **Pack the shoulder DOWN and BACK** before the elbow moves
- **Elbow drives past the ribs**, not flared wide
- Slow return, full stretch at the bottom

**LOAD:** 50 across all sets — strict, clean to rack, press straight up, NO push-press. **50 is the ceiling here, so the pause is the progression.**
- **2-3s PAUSE AT LOCKOUT on every rep** — bicep by the ear, shoulder packed DOWN, ribs down, and hold it. Either the position survives three seconds or it doesn't; there's no way to fudge it
- **Strict, ribs DOWN**, no rib flare
- Full lockout before the pause starts — don't start counting from a soft elbow
- Both sides to the same standard

It read *"pretty easy"* on Tuesday at this same 50. The pause is what makes it hard again without a heavier bell.

**LOAD:** Light bell (~20-30lb). **LEFT ARM FIRST — match the right to it.**
- **Upper arm pinned to the ribs**, elbow doesn't drift forward
- **Slow lower to a FULL stretch** — the bell loads the bottom where a dumbbell goes slack
- **Shoulder packed DOWN**, no shrug to start

🔥 Near-failure fine on the last set. Twice a week is the dose — this is frequency for the left arm, not intensity.

sets.name: 🌀🔆 Brutal Complex (@Asgooch) — 35, Rounds Are the Variable
sets.notes:
**LOAD: 35lb. Not a range — 35.** 3 rounds minimum, ~10-12 reps per move (each side where it alternates), circuit-style. Minimal rest between moves, ~60s between rounds.

swing → ab-stance goblet squat (alternate wide/narrow) → alternating bent-over row → close-grip pushup on the bell handles.

**Pace it by your own map:** the ab-stance squats and the close-grip pushups are the work; the swing and the row are the rest. Don't spend on the swings.

**🔆 The close-grip pushup is the spotlight — it's the beat with a real technique ceiling:**
- **Hands on the bell handles, elbows TUCKED to the ribs** — flaring them out on an unstable object is how the shoulder gets loaded in its worst position
- **Shoulders packed DOWN, ribs down**, body in one line — no sagging hips at the end of a round
- **Control the descent.** The bell wobbles; that instability is the training effect, and rushing it throws the effect away
- **Bail to the floor rather than grinding a collapsing rep** at the end of a round

**Rounds are the variable, not the bell.** Three is the target. Go past three if it's still there. **Stop a round when the hinge stops holding** — there's a bent-over row and loaded squats in here, and a broken hinge under fatigue is where this block would hurt you.

**Reflection:** at 35 across all three rounds, how does round three compare to last week's round three at 35-on-empty?

sets.name: Skill — Bent Press + Windmill 🛑
sets.notes: 2 rounds, unhurried. Light. This is skill practice at the end of a long day, not more work.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 25-35lb.
- **A HINGE and a side bend, not a press** — the arm locks out and stays locked; the body moves underneath it
- **Eyes on the bell** the whole way down
- **Hips go BACK and to the side**; come up by driving the hips, not pressing the arm
- Shoulder packed DOWN throughout 🛑

**LOAD:** 18-30lb, light.
- **Straight loaded arm, eyes on the bell**
- **Hinge to the opposite hip** — a hip hinge with rotation, not a side crunch
- Slow and controlled both directions

sets.name: Cooldown (Hip + Adductor + QL Release)
sets.notes: Give the QL the full beat — the complex loaded the hinge hard.

exercises.notes: Adductors — the ab-stance squats worked them.
30s each side. QL downshift, and Friday is legs.

tips: **35 on the complex. The block reads easy on paper and isn't** — the move list is familiar, the density isn't.
**Left arm first on the curl.** Twice a week is the point.
**Friday is legs.** If the complex leaves the QL tight, take the cool-down seriously.
